shortDescription: The German day-ahead electricity contract fell on Wednesday as wind power generation was set to pick up.($1 = 0.8754 euros)

children: The German day-ahead electricity contract fell on Wednesday as wind power generation was set to pick up.
The German day-ahead baseload power contract (TRDEBD1) fell 29% to €133 ($152) per megawatt hour at 0655 GMT, according to LSEG data.

"German wind power generation is expected to increase markedly tomorrow, reaching around 25 GW, before declining rapidly thereafter. Wind output should remain more limited in France," analysts at Engie's EnergyScan wrote in a note.

Wind power generation in Germany is expected to rise by 21.2 gigawatts to 28 GW, while solar power generation is set to fall by 4.4 GW to 11 GW. Consumption is expected to remain largely stable at 53.5 GW.
The equivalent French contract (TRFRBD1) was down 11.7% to €140/MWh.
Consumption, wind power and solar power generation were seen largely unchanged in France, falling by less than 1 GW each compared to Wednesday's levels.
French nuclear availability rose by 2 percentage points to 72% of total capacity.
The German month-ahead and Q4 2026 contracts were sitting at around €161/MWh and €165/MWh respectively, rising by about 2-3% each, according to LSEG data.
Along the curve, the German year-ahead contract (TRDEBYc1) edged down by 0.63% to €127/MWh.
The equivalent French contract (TRFRBYc1) was untraded, according to LSEG data.
The European carbon market's benchmark contract
was up 0.3% to €87.02 a metric ton.

title: German spot electricity contract falls on higher wind forecast
